evidence: src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:909 builds coerced_rows as [[_coerce_cell(row.get(c, "")) for c in columns] for row in rows] — each row list is generated by iterating over `columns`, so every row always has exactly len(columns) cells (missing keys default to ""), and cells are str via _coerce_cell (line 908 for column labels too). payload dict at 919-925 has keys 'columns' (list[str]), 'rows' (list[list[str]]), 'truncated' (int, 0 or total-lo at 950). _small_result_to_markdown (line 1201-1224) reads payload.get('columns')/'rows'/'truncated' and does zip(columns, rows[0], strict=True) at line 1220, which given the guaranteed equal-length rows from _compute_table_payload cannot raise ValueError from length mismatch.

In components_to_blocks (src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:331-344), the DATAFRAME branch calls `small = _small_result_to_markdown(payload)` at line 334 with no surrounding try/except. _build_table_payload (line 875) has its own internal broad except (referenced in the comment at lines 346-354), but that is a separate function call (line 332) that already returned before _small_result_to_markdown is invoked. No try/except wraps the _small_result_to_markdown call itself, so an exception it raises (e.g. ValueError from zip(strict=True) at line 1220 on a row/column-count mismatch) would propagate directly out of components_to_blocks rather than being caught and degraded to a skipped block.

src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:908 builds str_columns = [_coerce_cell(c) for c in columns] inside _compute_table_payload, and _coerce_cell (line 803-806) always returns str(value). The resulting payload's 'columns' key is consumed by _small_result_to_markdown (line 1210, called from line 334) which passes each column through _escape_small_result_text (line 1193, typed to accept str and calling value.replace(...)). Since columns are always str-coerced before reaching _escape_small_result_text, int/None column names cannot reach it un-stringified and cannot cause a failure.

In src/sqllens/tools/_format.py, candidates of type 'result_text' (created at line 336) are normalized to {'type':'text','text':cand['text']} at line 451-454 while building the 'blocks' list. query_results.html:752-767 creates the markdown-it renderer with { html:false, linkify:false, typographer:false, breaks:true } and no options disabling backslash-escapes or list parsing, so CommonMark defaults for both remain active; renderTextBlock (query_results.html:772-785) feeds block.text straight into markdownRenderer.render(). src/sqllens/tools/_format.py:50 defines _SMALL_RESULT_ESCAPED_CHARS = frozenset("\\`*_[]<>~|&"), covering every inline-opening character (backtick, *, _, [, ], <, >, |) plus backslash itself. _escape_small_result_text (line 1193-1198) backslash-prefixes each such char and flattens \r/\n to a space. _small_result_to_markdown (line 1201-1224) always renders each value after a fixed '**col:** ' (or '- **col:** ') prefix, so a value can never sit at true line-start; combined with newline flattening, this structurally blocks block-level markdown (headings '#', lists '-'/'1.'/'+', horizontal rules '---', tables, raw HTML blocks) regardless of leading characters, while the escaped charset blocks inline emphasis/code-spans/links/raw-HTML/pipes. No falsifying case found.
